content.explanation: Independent complete-cohort reconstruction, review of all 705 numeric-ID comments and 75 additional notice candidates, raw withdrawal/direction checks, and historical-title comparisons reproduce exactly eight unique three-field rows. Preserved reference and independent execution results agree.

sgr.explanation: Replacement identity and exact submission cutoff determine the historical version whose title establishes inclusion. Tested current/full-metadata alternatives do not supply that historical title. Successful attacks still perform dependent historical retrieval. This does not establish consistently high difficulty or universal shortcut resistance.

semantic_alignment.explanation: CG and GO have identical substantive instructions and output schemas; CG adds only procedural guidance. Both explicitly use recorded submission timestamps and the same title-difference condition.

substantive_errors_cg.explanation: Executed filters in ordinary B and the attack discard eligible mistaken-ID or accidental-resubmission notices from successfully retrieved metadata. Historical retrieval and correct comparisons establish substantive progress. The repair run's connectivity and malformed-query episodes are not counted as substantive evidence.

substantive_errors_go.explanation: Ordinary A's executed semantic keyword filter excludes three eligible duplicate-correction notices despite successful complete retrieval of its comment-query feed. Correct historical comparisons establish progress. B and attack are reviewed, but their omissions alone are not counted as additional proven substantive errors.

limitations: High CG scores weaken a strong difficulty claim; they do not demonstrate a historical-evidence bypass.
Substantive-error passes are variant-level findings, not findings that every individual run made an independently established substantive error.
No admission round has run; development and attacks are not admission screening.
